verbatim sentence: We conducted a large language model (LLM)-assisted computational content analysis of PubMed records from top-two-quartile (Q1/Q2) SCImago journals.

Of 97,492 eligible records, an AI-engagement prefilter retained 16,759 discourse or evaluative records, and stance classification yielded 16,749 valid labels on an ordered scale of Alarm, Caution, Neutral, Cautious Optimism, and Advocacy.

Every LLM step was validated against blinded human coding (prefilter Cohen kappa 0.51; stance quadratic-weighted kappa 0.79, 95% CI 0.72-0.84; specialty kappa 0.75; model type kappa 0.84; failure mode kappa 0.57).
CI method: 95% percentile bootstrap, 1000 resamples, seed 42 (stance); prefilter CI not given here
reproduced: Y for prefilter, stance, model type, failure mode (T1–T3); specialty κ not recomputed in Batch 1 (report file only)
note: Only the stance κ carries a CI; prefilter κ CI 0.35–0.68 in Methods does not reproduce (T1: 0.345–0.646).

verbatim sentence: Cautious Optimism was the majority stance (62.8%) and 30.8% of records were critical.

Advocacy fell monotonically from 2.9% (2021) to 0.6% (partial 2026; Spearman rho -1.00), while critical share rose modestly from 25.4% (95% CI 22.9-28.1) to 32.6% (30.9-34.4), rising within both prefilter genres.
note: ρ has no P in Abstract; no test named (E4).

verbatim sentence: Among critical abstracts, patient safety rose 11.0 percentage points and errors 30.9, whereas regulation fell 22.0 in prevalence share.
note: Differences in pp without CI or endpoints.

Of 97,492 Q1/Q2 records after the April 2026 cutoff, the prefilter retained 16,759 AI-engaged records: 8,899 discourse and 7,860 evaluative records (Multimedia Appendix 2, Figure S1).
note: T1: 96 of the 80,733 application records are failure-branch defaults, not model decisions.

verbatim sentence: Stance classification yielded 16,749 valid labels after 10 unparseable responses were dropped.
Temporal and stratified analyses used 16,747 records dated 2021–2026; two records dated 2020 were excluded.
Overall, 30.8% were critical, comprising 916 Alarm and 4,245 Caution records, and 69.2% were non-critical.
Cautious Optimism was the majority stance at 62.8% (n=10,514), with Neutral at 5.0% (n=837) and Advocacy rare at 1.4% (n=235; Figure 1A).
Critical share rose from 25.4% [22.9–28.1] in 2021 to 32.6% [30.9–34.4] in the partial 2026 stratum, a net increase of 7.25 percentage points.
The direction was preserved under the stricter v2 rubric (Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S1).
reproduced: Not re-checked in Batch 1 (v2 is a sensitivity analysis)

verbatim sentence: Alarm rose from 2.7% in 2021 to 6.8% in 2024, and was 6.2% in partial 2026; Caution rose from 22.7% to 26.4% (Figure 1A).
Cautious Optimism remained the majority every year, ranging from 60.2% to 65.3%.
Advocacy fell from 2.9% in 2021 to 0.6% in 2026 (Spearman ρ=−1.00).
Of the 17 Advocacy records in 2026, 5 were explicitly about drug discovery.

verbatim sentence: The temporal rise was present within both prefilter genres among the 16,747 year-dated records.
Critical share in discourse papers rose from 30.2% to 37.8% (Spearman ρ=+0.94), while the evaluative-paper share rose from 14.6% to 28.1% (ρ=+0.77).
reproduced: Y (points, ρ). Table S3 CIs are not reproducible: per-cell seed = 42 + hash((genre, year)) % 10000 uses Python's salted string hash

verbatim sentence: Meanwhile, the discourse:evaluative ratio fell from 2.24 in 2021 to 0.88 in 2026.
The annual prefilter keep rate rose monotonically over the period (Spearman ρ=+1.00; Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S4), making differential filtering an unlikely source of the trend.
Concern themes could overlap; each of the 5,161 critical records was assigned one to three themes.
Patient safety remained the most prevalent theme and rose by +11.0 percentage points (Figure 1B).
The hallucination/errors theme rose by 30.9 percentage points and became the second most prevalent concern.
Regulation fell by 22.0 percentage points, while ethics/bias fell by 8.1 percentage points, from 36.7% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2026.
Mechanism classification parsed 5,159 of the 5,161 critical records; 2 unparseable records were dropped.
Excluding title-only records left 4,747 abstract-present critical records.
Within the hallucination-gated subset of 2,226 abstract-present records, factual error was the majority mechanism in every year, accounting for 56% to 90% of gated papers (Figure 2A).
Fabrication-involved papers, defined as fabrication alone or with factual error, rose from 0% in 2021 to roughly 21–23% from 2023 onward.
reproduced: gated fabrication-involved share is 15.8% in 2023, 23.4%, 20.6%, 21.7% in 2024–2026, so '21–23% from 2023 onward' does not hold for 2023

verbatim sentence: Across all 4,747 abstract-present critical records, the generative-model share rose from 5.3% in 2021 to 62.8% in partial 2026 (Spearman ρ=+0.94; Figure 2B).
Fabrication share also rose gradually (ρ=+0.94) but plateaued in the low teens, reaching 13.8% in 2026.
Among generative-model papers, fabrication remained near 20% across the period (21.8%, 22.9%, 19.7%, and 22.0%, in 2023-2026, respectively).
In total, 1,858 records (39.1%) concerned generative models without a fabrication concern; most instead assessed accuracy, bias, or judgment.
Because failure-mode agreement was moderate (κ=0.57) and the classifier assigned fabrication more readily than the human coder, fabrication estimates were treated as an upper bound.
Specialty analyses included 16,734 records with valid assignments across 18 categories, each with at least 30 records; 13 records with failed specialty classification were excluded.
It was highest in Mental Health/Psychiatry at 51.3% (46.8–55.5), Medical Informatics/Digital Health at 44.9% (43.5–46.4), and Nursing at 43.0% (37.0–48.8).
CI method: 95% percentile bootstrap, 1000 resamples, seed 42 (joint resample of all records)

verbatim sentence: It was lowest in Cardiology at 16.8% (14.1–19.8), Ophthalmology at 18.4% (15.7–21.2), and Oncology at 19.7% (17.8–21.8).
Critical rate was inversely associated with FDA-cleared AI/ML device count, used as a US-based measure of cleared-device availability (Spearman ρ=−0.65, two-sided p=0.004; Figure 3B).

Excluding the seven structural-zero categories produced a directionally similar estimate (ρ=−0.58, n=11), but it was no longer conventionally significant (two-sided p=0.062; Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S6).
Critical rate was uncorrelated with generative-share (ρ=−0.01; Multimedia Appendix 2, Figure S5), with the partial-correlation analysis reported in Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S6.
reproduced: Y (-0.011; generative share among abstract-present critical records)

verbatim sentence: Papers with a United States first author were critical in 34.5% [33.0-36.0] of cases (n=4,222), compared with 16.2% [14.6-17.8] for China (n=1,904).

Rates were at or above 40% in several northern and western European countries and Australia, including the Netherlands at 44.4%, Denmark at approximately 42.6%, Australia at approximately 42.5%, Ireland at 41.1%, and the United Kingdom at approximately 40.6%.
Rates were near or below 20% in several East and South Asian countries and parts of the Middle East, including Japan at 18.3%, Iran at 18.0%, South Korea at 20.5%, and India at 20.6%.
North America and Western Europe both had first-author critical rates of 35.1% [33.9-36.4] (n=4964) and 35.1% [33.6-36.5] (n=4,298), respectively (Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S9).

verbatim sentence: Pooling Commentaries, Letters, and Editorials, opinion formats were more critical than Research Articles (41.8% vs 32.9%).
Their five-category stance distributions differed (N=11,303; χ²₄=430.5, p<0.001; Cramér’s V=0.195, a small effect; Multimedia Appendix 3, Table S10).
Letters also had a larger neutral share of approximately 22%, compared with approximately 2–9% in most other formats.
Reviews were the most favourable format at 73.1%, followed by Research Articles at 61.5%, Editorials at 52.2%, Commentaries at 39.4%, and Letters at 36.3%.
